title: Mathematical Geography - Grade 10-12 Worked Problems
fullText:
MATHEMATICAL GEOGRAPHY
Q1. Draw and label a longitude of 60˚W and another 30˚W.

Q5. What is the angle of elevation of the midday sun Berlin 46˚N when it is 22nd December?
Formula: Constant Angle = (known angle – degree of occurrence)
90˚= (46˚N + 23 ˚S)
90˚= 69 ˚
89.10-69.05 = 90˚ - 69 ˚
= 20 ˚ So angle of elevation of the midday sun is 20 ˚

Q11. What is the longitude of a place whose local time is 12:00 hours when Greenwich Time is 16:00hours?

Q14. At what latitude is the angle of elevation 90˚ at noon on 22nd December?
Formula: Constant Angle = (known angle – degree of occurrence)
90˚= (90˚- 23 ˚S)
90˚= 66 ˚
89.10-66.05 = 90˚ - 66 ˚
= 23 ˚ So latitude is 23 ˚

Q16. What would be the angle of elevation for a country along the latitude 60˚N when the sun is overhead on the tropic of cancer?
Formula: Constant Angle = (known angle – degree of occurrence)
90˚= (60˚N - 23 ˚N)
90˚= 36 ˚
89.10-36.05 = 90˚ - 36 ˚
= 53 ˚ So angle of elevation is 53 ˚

Q18. At 13:00 hours local time people in Ghana 60˚W were on a live WhatsApp broadcast of swearing in ceremony of a new elected president in a country where the local time is 09:00 hours. What is the longitude of the place where the ceremony was taking place?

_source: Real worked-example problem set (18 questions with full worked solutions) on Mathematical Geography -- longitude/latitude, local and standard time calculations, angle of elevation of the midday sun, and great-circle distance calculations -- the same sub-topic area as this app's existing Geography Grade 10-12 syllabus files (10.2.3 Latitude and Longitude / 10.2.4 Local and Standard Time / 10.2.6 apparent movement of the sun). This is a standalone worked-problems document, not organised into terms/topics/competencies of its own, so rather than force it into the syllabus schema it is bundled here as background grounding text only (per this app's 2026-09-15 pamphlet system), never shown in any picker or list. Reproduced as extracted (each question's diagram is described in the source as a row of degree/time labels either side of a 'W'/'E' axis, which does not survive PDF text extraction as a real diagram -- left as the source's own plain-text layout rather than redrawn or invented). Cleaned only of repeated PDF page-number artifacts and un-escaped PDF-to-text markdown artifacts (e.g. '\=' -> '=').
